meta.audience: The multitude, turned back to after the twelve
meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The sermon at the temple (3 Nephi 12–14)
principles: A measure that returns to the one who used it
Two houses in the same weather

world_behind.title: The audience turns back
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says he turned again to the multitude, after 3 Nephi 13:25 had narrowed the sermon to the twelve. The chapter is spoken to the whole crowd again from its first sentence.

world_behind.title: This chapter stays closest to the King James text
world_behind.text: Where 3 Nephi 12 alters forty-five of its forty-eight verses against Matthew 5, this one alters twelve. Most of what moves is the relative pronoun, with "which" becoming "who" in six separate verses.

world_behind.title: The opening frame is the one substantial addition
world_behind.text: Verse 1 supplies a sentence Matthew 7 does not have, reporting the turn to the multitude and the opening of his mouth. Everything after it follows the King James chapter closely.

world_behind.title: Matthew's closing verses are absent
world_behind.text: Matthew 7:28 and 29 record the crowd astonished at his doctrine and the reason given for it. The record stops this chapter at the equivalent of Matthew 7:27 and runs straight on into 3 Nephi 15.

world_behind.title: The sermon belongs to one unbroken day
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 11 through 18 is a single visit, and 3 Nephi 19:2 has word carried through the night for a second gathering the next morning. This chapter sits in the middle of a session that runs from the descent to the sacrament without a break.

world_behind.title: The phrase has only two other homes in the record
world_behind.text: "False prophets" appears at Words of Mormon 1:16, here at verse 15, and at 4 Nephi 1:34, where priests and false prophets lead the people to build many churches. The warning is quoted from Matthew and lands on a problem this record reports on both sides of it.

words.text: To measure out. The word occurs once in the record and six times in the King James Bible, three of them in this saying. Verse 2 makes the act of measuring reciprocal.
A speck. All three of the record's uses are in this chapter, and all six of the King James Bible's are in this same saying in Matthew and Luke.
Precious stones from the sea. The record uses the word twice, here and at 4 Nephi 1:24, where pearls mark the return of pride. The King James Bible has it eight times.
Treated at 1 Nephi 21:20, in quoted Isaiah, where it means narrow or cramped. Verse 13 sets it against wide and broad, and verse 14 pairs it with narrow.
Ravenous, tearing. It appears once in the record, and five times in the King James Bible. It sits inside the image of wolves in sheep's clothing.
Thorny weeds. One use here against three in the King James Bible, including Genesis 3:18, where they are part of the curse on the ground.

phrases.term: He turned again to the multitude
phrases.text: Mormon marking the audience shift back. The twelve had been addressed directly since 3 Nephi 13:25.

phrases.term: With what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again
phrases.text: The standard applied becomes the standard received. Verse 2 gives the mechanism behind the command in verse 1.

phrases.term: Considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye
phrases.text: The disproportion stated as a question. The speck and the beam are the same problem at different scales.

phrases.term: First cast the beam out of thine own eye
phrases.text: The order given, with the second step kept. The point is sequence rather than silence.

phrases.term: Neither cast ye your pearls before swine
phrases.text: The one verse in the section on judgment that counsels discrimination. It sits directly after the instruction not to judge.

phrases.term: Ask, and it shall be given unto you
phrases.text: Three verbs and three promises. James 1:5 turns the same promise toward one specific request.

phrases.term: All things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them
phrases.text: The rule stated positively, as something to do rather than to avoid. Verse 12 calls it the law and the prophets.

phrases.term: Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life
phrases.text: The narrow way described without apology. 2 Nephi 9:41 adds who keeps the gate.
The warning about appearance. The clothing is the disguise and the appetite is the fact.

phrases.term: I never knew you; depart from me, ye that work iniquity
phrases.text: The refusal given to people who list works done in his name. Mosiah 26:27 has the same sentence in the same form.

phrases.term: It fell not, for it was founded upon a rock
phrases.text: The identical weather falls on both houses. Only the foundation differs, and verse 27 gives the other outcome.

verses.label: v. 1–27
verses.title: Mostly pronouns
verses.text: Twelve of this chapter's twenty-seven verses carry a real word change, forty-four per cent, which ranks it nineteenth of the twenty-four quoted blocks. Nine of the seventeen edits are pronoun swaps: which to who six times, plus whom to who, whosoever to whoso, and that to which. Strip those and four substantive changes are left in the chapter, at verses 4, 5, 7 and 18, none of which alters a claim.

verses.label: v. 1–27
verses.title: How the three chapters differ
verses.text: The three chapters of this sermon were not handled alike, and the difference is easiest to see in what was added. 3 Nephi 12 inserts material at thirty-seven points, 3 Nephi 13 at three, and this chapter at two, one of which is the narrative frame in verse 1. Rates of change fall the same way, ninety-four per cent, then fifty-three, then forty-four. Whatever produced this text worked hardest on the chapter about the law and the beatitudes and left the chapter of proverbs and warnings very nearly as it stood.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: Back to the multitude
verses.text: Thirty-four words are set in front of "Judge not, that ye be not judged": "when Jesus had spoken these words he turned again to the multitude, and did open his mouth unto them again, saying: Verily, verily, I say unto you." Matthew has no such seam. Read together with the insertion at 3 Nephi 13:25, where he turns aside to the twelve, this one closes a bracket. Exactly ten verses, 3 Nephi 13:25 through 34, are marked off as spoken to the twelve alone, and everything before and after is addressed to the crowd.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: Three prepositions removed
verses.text: The King James mote and beam are pulled and cast out of the eye three times: "pull out the mote out of thine eye," "cast out the beam out of thine own eye," "cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye." Each of the three loses its first out here, giving "pull the mote out," "cast the beam out," "cast the mote out." Nothing else in the two verses moves. The doubled preposition was redundant in the King James and the redundancy is gone, which is a copy editor's change rather than a teacher's.

verses.label: v. 7
verses.title: The triplet made even
verses.text: Matthew's three promises do not match: "it shall be given you," but "it shall be opened unto you." One word is added here so that the first reads "it shall be given unto you," and the sentence becomes regular across all three clauses. It is the only insertion in the chapter apart from the frame at verse 1, and it changes nothing except the rhythm.

verses.label: v. 18
verses.title: One modal dropped
verses.text: The King James verse denies two possibilities with two verbs: "A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit." Here the second can is deleted, leaving "neither a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit." The first half still says the good tree is unable; the second half, having lost its own modal, borrows it, and the sentence is a shade less firm about the corrupt tree than the King James is.

verses.label: v. 27
verses.title: Where the sermon stops
verses.text: Matthew 7 has twenty-nine verses; this chapter has twenty-seven. The two that are absent are Matthew's own closing narration, that the people were astonished at his doctrine and that he taught as one having authority and not as the scribes. Both are the evangelist's comment rather than the sermon, and neither would fit a setting with no scribes in it. The chapter ends on the house that fell, and the narrator picks up again in the next chapter instead.

chapter.title: The command against judging comes with a reason
chapter.text: Verse 2 makes it self-executing. The standard is not withheld; it is returned.

chapter.title: Correction is delayed, not cancelled
chapter.text: Verse 5 still ends with removing the brother's mote. The chapter is about order of operations.

chapter.title: Discrimination survives the command
chapter.text: Verse 6 asks them to tell dogs and swine from others. Not judging and not discerning are held apart.

chapter.title: The rule is put positively
chapter.text: Verse 12 says do, where the same principle is often stated as a prohibition. It is also called the whole of the law and the prophets.

chapter.title: Few find the narrow way, and it is said plainly
chapter.text: Verse 14 offers no softening. The numbers are given as part of the description.

chapter.title: Fruit brackets the section on prophets
chapter.text: Verses 16 and 20 both say they will be known by their fruits. Everything between is the argument for it.

chapter.title: Works in his name are not sufficient
chapter.text: Verse 22 lists prophecy, exorcism, and wonderful works, and verse 23 refuses them. What is required in verse 21 is doing the Father's will.

chapter.title: The weather is identical
chapter.text: Verses 25 and 27 give the same rain, floods, and winds. The chapter's last argument is that the storm is not the variable.

applications.title: Set the standard you want applied to you
applications.text: The measure you use is the measure you get. Before criticising, decide whether you would accept the same audit.

applications.title: Do the beam first, then help
applications.text: The instruction ends with removing the mote rather than with leaving the person alone. Self-correction is the precondition for the help, and it does not stand in for it.

applications.title: Do all three verbs
applications.text: Ask, seek, knock, and then the same three repeated as promises. The three are distinct acts: a request, a search, and persistence at a closed door. Work out which of the three you have actually been doing.

applications.title: Turn the rule around and act
applications.text: The instruction is stated as something to do rather than something to avoid: "all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them." Take a thing you have been wishing someone would do for you, and do it for someone else this week.

applications.title: Expect the narrow way to be uncrowded
applications.text: The wide gate is described by its traffic and the narrow one by its scarcity, "few there be that find it." Popularity is offered here as evidence of nothing. If a course seems right and nobody is on it, that is the description, not a warning.

applications.title: Test by output over time
applications.text: Fruit takes a season. The chapter refuses to judge by appearance and refuses to judge quickly; give it long enough for something to grow.

applications.title: Watch the gap between saying and doing
applications.text: "Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord... but he that doeth the will of my Father." The people rejected in this passage are inside the vocabulary and outside the practice. Check where your own language runs ahead of your conduct.

applications.title: Assume the same weather
applications.text: Both houses got the rain. Plan for the storm on the assumption it is coming to you as well, and let the difference be in what you are standing on.

questions.text: What judgment of mine would I be uncomfortable receiving?
What beam have I stopped noticing?
What have I offered to people who could not receive it?
What have I stopped asking for?
What would I want done to me in the situation I am in now?
What am I saying that I am not doing?
What is my house actually built on?

entries.head: 3 Ne. 13:25

anchor.quote: he turned again to the multitude

entries.reason: the eleven verses spoken to the twelve alone

targets.quote: he looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen, and said unto them:
targets.verse_text: And now it came to pass that when Jesus had spoken these words he looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen, and said unto them: Remember the words which I have spoken. For behold, ye are they whom I have chosen to minister unto this people. Therefore I say unto you, take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
targets.markdown: And now it came to pass that when Jesus had spoken these words **he looked upon the twelve whom he had chosen, and said unto them**: Remember the words which I have spoken. For behold, ye are they whom I have chosen to minister unto this people. Therefore I say unto you, take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
